title: Empower Post-hoc Graph Explanations with Information Bottleneck: A Pre-training and Fine-tuning Perspective

problem.claim: Post-hoc explanation methods need to explain Graph Neural Networks while balancing explanation fidelity and intelligibility.

gap.claim: Task-specific methods depend on accessible downstream tasks and target-model outputs, limiting explanation of pretrained GNNs, transferable knowledge, and internal representations.

contributions.claim: A two-stage strategy pretrains explainers task-agnostically in representation space and fine-tunes them jointly in label and representation spaces when downstream tasks are accessible.

The Explainable Graph Information Bottleneck framework unifies task-specific and task-agnostic explanation through an Information Bottleneck objective, with a tractable bound and an explanation-generation architecture.
Task-agnostic explanation is theoretically shown to be a relaxed sufficient condition for task-specific explanation, indicating transferability.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the two-stage strategy applies to pretrained GNNs with inaccessible downstream tasks and can explain transferable knowledge.
The authors report that representation-space explanations provide finer-grained information.
Extensive experiments are reported to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed explanation method.

narrative_sequence.summary: Existing graph explanation methods face limited applicability and insufficiently fine-grained explanations.
The paper introduces a two-stage explanation strategy spanning task-agnostic representation-space pretraining and optional task-specific fine-tuning.
EGIB uses the Information Bottleneck principle to unify explanation settings and address fidelity–intelligibility trade-offs.
A theoretical result characterizes task-agnostic explanation as a relaxed sufficient condition for task-specific explanation.
The authors report extensive experiments demonstrating effectiveness.

source_observation.claim: Explanation in representation space is presented as applicable when downstream tasks are inaccessible and as more fine-grained than label-space-only explanation.

interpretation.claim: When task labels or downstream objectives are unavailable, intermediate representations may provide a transferable explanatory target.

application.claim: For pretrained graph models, consider task-agnostic representation-space explanation before optional task-specific adaptation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that representation-space explanations are preferable for every model, task, or user need.

source_observation.claim: EGIB combines task-specific and task-agnostic explanation under an Information Bottleneck framework.

interpretation.claim: A unified objective can support explanation across different levels of task access while explicitly managing fidelity and intelligibility.

application.claim: Design explanation systems with a shared objective that can specialize according to whether downstream task information is available.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the operational trade-off, optimization costs, or conditions under which the unified framework is advantageous.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative experimental results are unspecified.
The tractable bound, explanation-generation architecture, and theoretical assumptions are unspecified.
The scope and conditions of downstream-task accessibility are unspecified.
